San Francisco Planning, Article 10 landmark designation: Landmark No. 210, Murphy Windmill and Millwright's Cottage (ordinance, Planning Commission resolution and case report)
sources.label: SF Planning, landmark designation

historical_record.description: Designated San Francisco Landmark No. 210, Murphy Windmill and Millwright's Cottage.

The millwright's cottage was built between December 1909 and early 1910, designed free of charge by the Reid Brothers — architects of the Hotel del Coronado — as a free-standing Georgian Revival cottage with "Dutch" and Arts and Crafts touches, meant by the Park Commission to harmonise with the windmill; a rare type in the city.
The millwright Charles Kamp lived in the cottage for twenty-nine years, keeping up the windmill long after electric pumps had taken over; millwrights had lived here since 1909.
